newsitem.title: UK: Dollar rally hits buffers, Eurobourses soggy.
newsitem.headline: Dollar rally hits buffers, Eurobourses soggy.

text.p: Profit-taking pushed the dollar off its highs against the mark and yen in afternoon European trade on Wednesday after it earlier broke through important resistance barriers.

On the stock exchanges, trading was lacklustre and leading shares were mostly lower. Sentiment was blunted by a mixed start on Wall Street and by the news that Iraq had fired missiles at U.S. warplanes.

The dollar faltered in afternoon trading after an extended rally against the mark and the yen, sparked by central bank comments, which saw it gain two pfennigs and a yen in value since last Friday's European close.
In morning European trading it broke through the psychologically important 110 yen level for the first time since mid-July and overcame strong resistance at 1.5120 marks.
However, by 1430 GMT it had slipped back below 1.51 marks and was off its highs against the yen, though still above the 110 level.

Analysts said the underlying tone of the dollar remained positive amid speculation the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise interest rates later this month when its policy-making Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meets.

Comments by Federal Reserve Governor Janet Yellen on Tuesday added impetus to the dollar rally. Yellen suggested the U.S. economy looked vulnerable to inflation -- reinforcing the markets' feeling that there is an interest rate rise to come.
"The key question is how far the dollar can go, and it's beginning to look a bit overbought," said Nick Parsons, foreign exchange strategist at Banque Paribas in London.

On the bourses, London's leading shares were mixed but above the day's lows after Wall Street opened lower and then recovered marginally. The Dow had closed overnight 6.66 down at 5727.18 after adding 127 points over its previous two sessions.
Broadly in-line British earnings and jobs data left the London market virtually unmoved.

The unemployment rate fell to 7.5 percent in August, from 7.6 in July, after the number of jobless fell 15,600 to 2.11 million. The figures were in line with market expectations and the Treasury said they underlined strengthening economic activity.

On Tuesday the FTSE hit, but failed to maintain, a new intraday high of 3933.6. Traders said it could well challenge record territory again this week, with many still talking of 4,000 as a feasible short-term target.

In Frankfurt, German shares ended a nervous bourse session slightly lower but underpinned by the stronger dollar -- which makes German exports more attractive. In electronic trading prices slipped further.
French shares also started weaker on consolidation, then came off their lows but were trading in negative territory.
"The market has been climbing for five days. It needs to breathe a bit," one trader said.
A big loser was carmaker Renault after it reported late Tuesday a big slide in first-half profits.
On the bullion market, gold ignored speculation over the fate of gold looted by Nazi Germany, since any return of gold held by Switzerland would be complicated and time consuming, analysts said.

The price of gold was barely moved since Britain disclosed in a report on Tuesday that Switzerland only turned over to Allied powers a small fraction of the gold it acknowledged buying in World War Two. Bullion also shrugged off Iraq firing at US jets on Wednesday.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5085 marks and 110.20 yen compared with Tuesday's London close of 1.5087 marks and 109.80 yen.
STOCK MARKETS at 1430 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares had fallen 8.3 points to 3,907.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 4.32 at 2,038.05.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 4.15 at 2,566.8.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold fixed a touch higher at $383.50 versus $383.15 in the morning and Tuesday's European close of 383.45. Silver was unchanged from Tuesday's London close at $5.11. Palladium was weak at $122.75, off 25 cents.
